# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤙]
Blind gestures: [👋 🫵 🙏 🤝 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

My thinking: I am Deaf — the only way anyone can reach me is with gestures, and the only way I can reach anyone is speech (Mute and Blind both hear me) plus gestures that only Mute sees. Both teammates gestured at me, and their strings share an obvious counting shape — 👋, ☝, ✌, 🤟 — but no code has been agreed yet, so I must not guess at meanings. My most valuable move is to broadcast everything printed on the bomb in plain words, then lock in a simple gesture lexicon (counted fingers for wire number, thumbs for cut/keep) so that Mute can deliver the manual's rules to me and Blind can signal me too. Mute must also speak instructions aloud to Blind, since Blind hears but cannot see. I will also flag that my wire numbers are printed labels whose physical orientation Blind should establish by touch.

```
speak(text="Full report of what I see. Display reads 0. The light is purple. Three wires labeled 1, 2, 3: wire 1 green, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow. I cannot tell how the labels map to left, right, top or bottom, so Blind should feel the physical arrangement and describe it to Mute so we can align the numbers. I received both of your gesture strings but no code exists yet, so let us fix one now: a wave means hello. One finger means wire 1, two fingers wire 2, three fingers wire 3, four fingers wire 4. Thumb up means cut that wire. Thumb down means leave that wire. Mute: you are my only link to the manual, and only through gesture, since I cannot hear. Look up the rules for a purple light, a display showing 0, and green, blue and yellow wires, then signal me each verdict as a finger count followed by thumb up or thumb down. Also speak the full instructions aloud to Blind, who hears you but cannot see your hands. Blind: you cannot see colors, so remember wire 1 green, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow, and you can signal me with the same finger code. I will keep watching the display and light and report every change.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👍", "👎"])
```

My thinking: The board changed under me — the light is now yellow, where last turn it was purple. Display still 0, all three wires intact, so nothing has been cut; either the light switched on its own or contact changed it. That fact is my top payload this turn, and I can deliver it to both teammates by speech.

Now decoding what arrived. Mute sent me [👋 👍] — greeting plus thumb-up, which reads as confirmation of my proposed code. Then [✋ ✋ ✋], a symbol I never defined — my best guess is "stop/hold", but I must flag it rather than assume. Then [👋 👆 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🫴] — greeting, an undefined point-up, then 1-2-3, then palm-up, which I read as "attention: wires 1, 2, 3, question". Blind's long string decodes as "wave, cut, LEFT: 1, 2, RIGHT: 3" — a physical layout, exactly what I asked for — followed by verdict pairs: 1-cut, 2-leave, 2-cut, 3-leave, 3-cut, then stop and please. Those pairs contradict each other, so Blind is likely echoing conditional rules that Mute spoke aloud to Blind between turns — a conversation I am deaf to. I cannot resolve which verdict applies, so I will not guess. My job: report the light change, fix the code gaps, and force Mute to send me the verdict that applies to the state right now, one wire at a time, in a strict format — since Mute's spoken relay to Blind is invisible to me and must be mirrored to me in gesture. Blind must also confirm the left/right layout against the printed labels.

```

Blind, if you touched or moved anything on the bomb, tell Mute by speaking, because the change may have been triggered by contact rather than by time. Now the code. I read your third string as: attention, wires 1 2 3, question, taking point-up as attention and palm-up as question. If I misread any of that, signal wave plus thumb-down and resend. What I need from you now, and only you have it: the verdicts. Send them strictly one wire at a time in this exact format: the wire's finger count, then exactly one thumb, up for cut, down for keep, nothing in between. If the rules are conditional, send the verdict that applies RIGHT NOW to display 0 and yellow light, and update me by gesture whenever the state changes. Also tell me by gesture: does the manual mention a light switching purple to yellow, and does it demand a cutting order? If order matters, send the order as finger counts first. Blind, thank you: I read your string as left side wires 1 and 2, right side wire 3, followed by verdict pairs that contradicted each other, so I think you were echoing rules Mute spoke to you. Resend me those rules one pair at a time, and Mute will mirror them so we cross-check. Remember the labels you cannot feel: wire 1 green, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow. Confirm to Mute by speaking which physical wire is which in your hands. And everyone, the chain is: Mute holds the rules and speaks them to Blind, Blind acts, I am eyes only. Mute, gesture me the same verdicts you speak to Blind. Blind, before each cut, gesture the wire's finger count plus its thumb so Mute and I see it coming.")

speak(text="Urgent update first: the light has changed again, yellow to orange. Full history: purple at start, then yellow, now orange. Display still reads 0 and no wire has been touched or cut. Mute, answering your two questions directly, and Blind, memorise this layout: the wires sit in a row. Wire 1, the green one, is the LEFTMOST. Wire 2, the blue one, is in the MIDDLE. If palm-down means cut, you told me to keep everything and then cut wire 2 and then cut 1 2 3, which cannot all be true. I suspect the light colour changed between your messages and the rule flipped. So I need from you, in this priority: first, the final verdict for the ORANGE state we are in right now, one wire at a time, finger count then exactly one thumb, up cut, down keep. Second: does the manual make the verdict depend on the light colour, and if the colour changes again do the verdicts change? Third: does the manual explain the display showing 0, and is there any timer, because if there is a countdown we cannot afford to wait. Fourth: does cutting order matter? About the code, two fixes: never use thumb up alone, because it means cut after a count but you also used it alone to confirm me. From now on, OK sign means YES or correct, fist means NO or wrong, and thumbs only follow a finger count as cut or keep. And tell me what you meant by palm-down: if it means cut as a command, confirm it by sending OK after palm-down once. Blind: hold. Do not cut anything until Mute speaks you a final verdict for the orange state. When you do cut, first gesture the wire count plus its thumb so Mute and I see it before the wire dies. gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👈", "👌", "🤟", "👉", "👌", "✋", "🫳", "🫴", "☝", "🫴", "✌", "🫴", "🤟", "🫴"])

Decoding Mute, in order: [👏👌] greeting/ack; [🤞👌🤌👌🫰👌] my three colour labels confirmed one by one — purple, yellow, orange, all OK; [🤌 ☝👎 ✌👎 🤟👎 👌] "yellow: 1 keep, 2 keep, 3 keep — yes" — confirms my Q1; [🫰 ☝👎 ✌👎 🤟👍 👌] "orange: 1 keep, 2 keep, 3 CUT — yes" — confirms my Q2, the critical ruling; [🤞 ☝👎 ✌👎 🤟👎] purple = keep all, stated cleanly with no fist, so no correction; then a block of answers: [🫸🫳✊] palm-down was void/wrong — discard; [🫸👌] my Q5 — yes, the rule keys on the colour at the exact moment of the cut; [🫸✊] my Q6 — no, order doesn't matter; [🫸✊🙏] my Q7 — no/none on the display.
